meters.label: Held on the card (whole currency units)
Paid to the merchant (rounded to whole units)

frames.narration: A customer orders goods for 100.00. The merchant asks its provider to authorize the card. The provider passes the request through the network to the issuer, the cardholder's bank.
The issuer approves and puts 100.00 on hold. The cardholder sees 400.00 available, but no charge is final and the merchant has no money. Nothing has moved between banks.
The first parcel ships. The merchant captures 40.00 of the authorization. The hold becomes a charge for that part, and the fee for this capture is 1.46.
Two days later settlement runs. The money moves between the banks and the provider pays the merchant 38.54, which is 40.00 less the fee. Until then the merchant's amount was pending.
The second parcel is cancelled. The merchant voids the rest of the hold, or the hold simply expires after the limit. Either way the customer gets 60.00 back, with no charge and no refund to wait for.
Later, a late capture of the cancelled amount is attempted. The provider rejects it, because the authorization was released. The merchant would have to authorize again.
The customer returns part of the first parcel. The merchant refunds 25.00. It is a new transaction after the capture, limited to the 40.00 captured, and the customer sees it as a separate credit.
